inputs.sequence_prompt:
One uninterrupted fifteen-second live-action shot starting exactly with the provided frame, on the SAME airship upper deck. Preserve the three real actors and all physical objects exactly. Setzer stands at the existing controls on the RIGHT, Celes stands in the CENTER, Locke stands behind her on the LEFT. Red masts, ropes, red wooden top rail, brass balusters, deck, control pedestal, existing brass lever and the city architecture remain the same. Do not add equipment, people, shields, weapons, wheels or handles. Preserve each costume precisely as visible in this frame, including Setzer's cream trousers and blue cuffs. Same mature silver-haired captain, blonde Celes with ponytail and blue ribbon in ivory dress and blue sash, brown-haired Locke with blue headband, dark jacket, cream shirt and boots. No identity or costume changes.
The actors have NATURAL HUMAN SKIN with the exact neutral warm beige and tan complexion of this corrected source. Preserve their skin color throughout all motion, including faces, ears, necks, arms, hands and fingers. Neutral soft light on skin; evening violet sky and red painted wood do not dye the people pink. Real skin texture with restrained natural saturation, no magenta illumination or red wash. Lighting remains steady with no flicker, flashing, bloom or glowing skin.
The engine is ALREADY running quietly. The airship is still docked at the beginning. From zero to five seconds, Setzer looks down at the EXISTING brass lever beneath his right glove and moves it a short distance smoothly to the next mechanical detent, keeping the same hand wrapped around the same handle. His other hand remains on the existing control. This starts a brief mechanical winch sound from the lower deck BELOW the frame, retrieving the boarding gangway. The gangway itself is below and out of view; do not invent a ramp inside this shot. Locke turns his head and upper body to look down toward the dock below the left side of the deck, checking the operation, with both feet still firmly planted. Celes watches Locke, then glances toward Setzer with an expectant expression. All three remain separate and grounded, without crossing paths.
From five to ten seconds, the winch stops with one firm latch click. The ship and city remain stationary until the check is complete. Locke finishes looking down, turns his face back toward Setzer, and clearly speaks the ONLY dialogue, in natural Brazilian Portuguese, with visible synchronized lips: <d>[Portuguese] Passarela recolhida. Podemos partir.</d> Celes reacts to his confirmation by widening her stance a little and placing her right hand on the nearest red wooden top rail, fingers closing naturally around the rail without passing through it. Setzer briefly acknowledges Locke with a small head turn, then faces forward. The captain listens; he does not speak or repeat the engine-start line.
From ten to fifteen seconds, ONLY AFTER Locke's complete confirmation, the low engine sound grows and the airship begins a gentle slow vertical lift. The camera is attached to the ship: the deck, masts, controls, railing and actors remain rigidly together. The distant city buildings slide downward slowly and coherently as a single real city, with natural depth parallax, not bending, melting, rotating or changing design. A subtle weight shift in Celes and Locke shows the start of movement; feet stay on deck and Celes's hand stays on the rail. They look outward toward the receding city with alert relief. Setzer stays in command at the same controls. Hair and clothes respond to a mild breeze; no violent wind or rocking. End during the living slow ascent, no freeze or fade.
Camera keeps the original viewing axis and full three-person composition. A very small smooth backward drift on the deck preserves head-to-boot visibility; no orbit, cut, zoom, new viewpoint or sudden camera move. No bodies or hands pass through equipment. Normal human movement, purposeful actions and responsive faces. The ship never moves before the gangway retrieval and spoken confirmation. Native sound: quiet engine from start, one short mechanical winch followed by latch click, Locke's single Portuguese line, then rising engine hum and restrained wind. No music, narration, singing or other speech.
